rulebook.title: The Void Throne — Player Rulebook, draft v0.3
blocks: The conquest has ended, but the ships, soldiers and institutions who made it possible still need a future. You have two months to show that your proposed government can work, then decide who will hold power when the emergency is over.
The Void Throne is a game of negotiation about governing a new interstellar empire. You will talk, make offers, write decisions into law… and then live with their consequences.
Two from Ductus Guild, which controls navigation and transport.
Two from the Janissariat, the army that won the war.
The Ascendant, the ruler who united the empire and can see the future.

You face one connected emergency: A space passage called the Narrow is deteriorating. The star system of Sorenne's Fall needs supplies, and a cohort of Janissariat needs transport, but your ships and forces cannot do every job.
At the same time, you are writing two parts of the empire's constitution: who directs transport between the stars, and who directs military operations.

Roughly two hundred inhabited worlds, stations and habitats form the Settled Dark. For three thousand years, six great dynastic Houses ruled it through the Conclave of Thrones, but over decades of conquest, a figure known only as the Ascendant broke their power.

The new empire is called the Settled Dominion and its rulers are negotiating a Charter of Settlement: the constitution that will define the institutions of the new order. The negotiations take place at the Seam - the ancient space station the Ascendant rules from.

Interstellar travel depends on Guild navigators, who learn to sense and interpret the immaterial deep through which ships travel. Owning a ship is not enough: you need their specialist expertise. The Ductus Guild uses that dependence to defend its licences, professional independence and commercial obligations.
The Guild's Navigation Rights Petition, called GUILD-14, has waited fourteen years for a formal answer in the Charter of Settlement.

The Janissariat is an enormous army of psychically conditioned warriors. That conditioning made them an effective instrument of war. It frays without fighting, weakening combat power and the habits that sustain imperial military authority.
That gives the army a difficult incentive: a peaceful month may help the Dominion while weakening the Janissariat in the future.
Little is known of the Ascendant, but that they appeared leading the Janissariat at the start of the conquest, and that they have the power of foresight.
The Ascendant begins with the right to issue imperial orders, but need support from the Guild and the Janissariat to enact those orders.

The Narrow is a strategic passage between dense stellar formations, linking the inner systems to the southern rim. Supplies passing through it sustain Sorenne's Fall, a star system of forty million people living beneath the debris of a battle fought before Pale Meridian.

Sorenne's Fall governs itself through the administration left behind when House Sorenne fell. The Sorenne Flag is the surviving fleet of the fallen house. It scattered rather than surrender at Pale Meridian and continues to resist the Dominion. It also delivers irregular supplies to Sorenne's Fall: destroying its ships would leave the system harder to govern.
Spear, a Janissariat cohort, is held at the Narrow while its commanders seek passage to the Flag's anchorage beyond it.
The Guild and the Janissariat each have two players. Each pair shares assets and objectives, but sit on different councils.
The Ascendant is a single player, supported by the army and able to spend their own power on foresight.
All three parties need to reach a settlement.
Navigation and Supply has one Guild delegate and one Janissariat delegate:
Security and Government has the other Guild delegate, the other Janissariat delegate and the Ascendant.
The game consists of two rounds, each representing a month. A round has five minutes of faction phase, a five minute council phase and a five minute free phase.
After the second round, there will be a ten-minute Ceremony of Settlement to resolve the new government.
Read your faction's Player Brief alongside these rules.

You have five minutes to decide your faction's approach. Discuss with your teammate from the start and use the time as you see fit. Guild and Janissariat players stay at their own faction tables and do not speak or send messages to the other faction during this phase. The Ascendant may visit either faction after making their foresight choice.
Your assets are the named ships or military units your faction controls.
An assignment is the job you give an asset for this round.
Agree one assignment for each asset, using the options printed on it.

The Ascendant first chooses a prophecy or chooses to save their foresight. They make that choice privately, before visiting either faction or hearing its plans for this round. They may then visit either table, discuss proposals and share information. You may revise your unlocked assignments in response. The Ascendant's Player Brief explains their powers.

You may revise your assignments until the end of the phase. Both teammates then confirm the same final assignments aloud and record them on one faction sheet. Take your approach to the councils yourselves; you do not need to write instructions to them. The Ascendant completes the faction-phase decisions described in their brief at the same deadline.

Assignments now lock for the round. In round two, a Standing Commitment may already fix an asset's assignment: this is a promise agreed and recorded during the previous free discussion. Mark that assignment LOCKED on your sheet.
If either teammate has not confirmed the assignments by the faction bell, or they disagree, use the faction's defaults:
Janissariat: Spear Stand down; Vigil Home.

A missing or multiple selection for an individual asset uses that asset's default. Lost or disabled assets are Absent. A Standing Commitment overrides a conflicting selection or default; withdrawing agreement later does not release it.

Go to your council and negotiate its action, called its order, using the assets offered. Your council reference lists the available orders, their requirements and their effects. Coordinate with the other council where one decision depends on the other.

Check the current article: the constitutional rule saying who has authority to choose the council's order. At the start, the Ascendant chooses both orders and tells each council their decision in person. Later articles may give that authority to a faction's representative or require both representatives to agree.

At the council bell, the players whose approval is required confirm the final order aloud. One council member records it for the facilitator. No initials or signatures are needed. Earlier proposals and informal promises do not replace this final decision. The Ascendant also completes the council-phase decision in their brief.

The facilitator resolves both councils, private assignments and scenario conditions, then announces track changes, asset losses, completed contracts and token expenditure. Neither council can change its order after seeing the other's result.

After round one, discuss what happened and what government you would like to try. Use the Charter options in the Component Reference to propose one Navigation article and one Military article. The two council representatives concerned and the Ascendant must agree an article aloud; the facilitator records the result. The two articles are decided separately. Where no agreement is reached, the existing arrangement continues.

You may attach a Standing Commitment to a proposed article to fix one of your faction's asset assignments for round two. Both teammates must agree that promise. Record the asset, assignment and article together; the Component Reference gives the permitted commitments and their conditions. Articles and attached commitments that pass govern round two.
After round two, use this discussion to negotiate the final settlement package. There is no further operation or recovery before the Ceremony.

After round two, freeze each party's weight and begin the ten-minute Ceremony. You are voting on a complete package: one Navigation article and one Military article. They need not be the articles tried provisionally.
Guild: 2 for an intact Wayfarer, 1 for surviving Lantern navigators, and 1 if Beacon is at least 1.
Ascendant: final Readiness plus unspent foresight.

Readiness sustains both the army's institutional power and the ruler's authority, so losing it weakens both signatures. Contracts and reserve tokens add no weight. Weight cannot be transferred between parties.

On the final settlement sheet, tick one box beside each player's role: Assent or Do not assent. Both Guild players must assent for the Guild's weight to count; both Janissariat players must assent for the army's weight to count. The Ascendant assents individually. An unticked row or disagreement within a faction gives that party no supporting weight. No handwritten signatures are needed.

Add all available weight, including parties that refuse or abstain. The package needs at least two-thirds of that total, rounded up, and signatures from at least two parties with positive weight. A total weight of zero cannot ratify a settlement.

Example: Guild 4, Janissariat 3 and Ascendant 4 give eleven in total. Two-thirds rounds up to eight. Guild and Ascendant can pass a package with eight; Guild and Janissariat have only seven. If the Guild players split, their faction contributes no support, but its four stays in the total.
There is no automatic veto. A package can therefore pass over a party's refusal and impose duties on that party.

If the first package fails, negotiate a replacement before the deadline. Collect fresh votes whenever either article changes; previous approvals do not carry over. You may hold up to two ballots. Stop when a package passes.
If no package passes, both provisional articles expire and both councils return to Interim. Interim is the fallback, not an option on the final ballot.

The physical result remains: lost assets stay lost, tracks stay where they finished and spent foresight does not return. Ratification settles the articles, but the people governing Sorenne's Fall will have to live with what those decisions have done.

What government did you want at the start, and what did you accept at the end? Name a decision or event that changed your view. What did your faction give up, what did it receive, and what did your teammate contribute?

For the Ascendant, did foresight change a decision, a bargain or only your confidence? One remaining token is inevitable after two purchases. Declining a purchase is the choice that preserves more power.
Design by John Keyworth. Paper prototype v0.3, revised 14 October 2026. Use the current player rulebook and facilitator guide together; earlier packs retain superseded foresight and settlement rules.

facilitator.title: The Void Throne — Facilitator Guide, draft v0.3
blocks: The Void Throne — Facilitator Guide, draft v0.3

Run the two-month crisis and make the consequences legible. Players decide what to offer, which orders to issue, and what government they will accept. Apply the printed outcomes. Do not invent a prophecy, a resource, another player's agreement, an extra veto or a reward for cooperation.

[WORKING] This guide implements the revised visions, Trial A Standing Commitments and weighted final settlement. The computer model is an implementation to check, not permission to overrule the paper rules. The browser is an all-seat facilitator test bench; the preserved LLM run is separate evidence.

One player rulebook, one Component Reference, one facilitator guide and three shared-role briefs. The Ascendant's brief includes their complete foresight, Warrant and reserve rules. Give each council the relevant action and Charter references from the Component Reference.
Two council reference sheets and four asset cards: Wayfarer, Lantern, Spear and Vigil.
Six Charter cards: three Navigation articles and three Military articles.

Four vision covers and four concealed answers: Navigation and Supply, and Security and Government for each round. The covers name the councils only. Keep the descriptive titles, questions and conditional effects inside the answers.
Three tracks numbered 0–4, with one counter each; three foresight tokens; one reserve token for Grey Petrel.
Four faction sheets and four council sheets: one for each faction and council in each round.
Two Ascendant worksheets, one provisional-government proposal and outcome record, two final-package ballot sheets, and a public record for results and contracts.
Blank paper can replace a decision sheet if it records the same choices and outcomes. Use the current vision and settlement rules with any older printed components.

Place Navigation and Supply at one end and Security and Government at the other. Keep the tracks, current articles and final decisions in a central space where everyone can read them. Provide separate places for the Guild and Janissariat to confer during the faction phase. The Ascendant begins apart from both factions, with the foresight covers.

Seat GN and JN at Navigation and Supply; GS, JS and A at Security and Government. Give both members of each faction their shared brief. Keep the four private vision answers behind your screen; put both current-round covers face up at the start of faction discussion.

Give Wayfarer and Lantern to the Guild, and Spear and Vigil to the Janissariat. All four assets begin available. Give the Ascendant three foresight tokens and Grey Petrel's reserve token. The facilitator keeps the vision answers concealed.

Set Beacon to 2, Sorenne's Fall's Stability to 3 and Readiness to 3. The Guild has completed no contracts. Write Interim in both article spaces: the Ascendant chooses both council orders, while the factions control their own assets.
The starting settlement weights are Guild 4, Janissariat 3 and Ascendant 6. If those values remained unchanged, nine of the total thirteen weight would be required to pass a settlement.

The faction sheet records the round and one agreed assignment for each asset. Both teammates confirm their choices aloud; no signatures are needed. Representatives take their faction's approach to the councils themselves, without written instructions or requests.

The council sheet records the round, current article and final order. Check spoken agreement from whoever holds authority under that article; do not collect initials. The Ascendant confirms their decisions in person. Record their foresight choice, reserve task and final Warrant on their worksheet.

The public record shows the three tracks, available assets, completed contracts, remaining tokens, current articles and binding commitments. Faction drafts and current plans stay with their faction; do not announce them before the Ascendant's choice. Publish final assignments when the faction phase ends. The Ascendant learns current plans through visits after choosing, not through a compulsory statement of intentions.
Allow eight minutes for the briefing. Explain the factions, the two councils and the crisis before taking the players through a round.

The crisis concerns Sorenne's Fall, the southern star system of forty million people described in the lore, and the Sorenne Flag, House Sorenne's surviving fleet. Stability measures the system's supplies and functioning services, not its loyalty. The Flag also makes irregular supply deliveries there; military disruption can therefore harm the people the Dominion is trying to govern. For this scenario, their supply route uses the Narrow, Spear seeks passage to a Flag anchorage beyond it, and a Flag patrol supplies the local Raid target. Those deployments are scenario additions. Players remain at the Seam; each round represents one month.

0–8: briefing. 8–13: round-one faction discussion. 13–18: councils and resolution. 18–23: discuss the result and agree provisional articles. 23–28: round-two faction discussion. 28–33: councils and resolution. 33–38: free discussion. 38–48: Ceremony. Use the remaining twelve minutes for the debrief. These five-minute discussion phases follow the current player rulebook.

The faction phase has one five-minute deadline. Guild and Janissariat players talk only to their own teammates and cannot send messages to the other faction. They begin immediately and budget their time themselves. The Ascendant first chooses one prophecy or NONE privately, using the public state and earlier discussions, before visiting either faction or receiving its current plans. Do not call minute-two or minute-three gates or require factions to announce intentions.

Record the Ascendant's choice before allowing visits. Pay before dealing the exact answer; publish expenditure and remaining foresight, not the chosen council. A choice completes that round's opportunity: no swaps or second purchase. NONE also permits visits. Record NONE if no single valid choice arrives before the phase ends. After choosing, the Ascendant may visit either faction, revisit it, relay offers and share the vision. Do not combine the factions into a table discussion. Unlocked assignments and Grey Petrel's task remain revisable until the faction deadline; the clock does not restart.

At the faction bell, ask both faction members to confirm the same assignments. Record one final faction sheet. If either has not confirmed or they disagree, apply the faction defaults; an activated Standing Commitment still overrides them. Mark unavailable assets Absent and record one reserve task. At the council bell, check the current authority and ask the required decision-makers to confirm the final order; also confirm the Warrant. Resolve the recorded decisions. No signatures or initials are needed.

In the browser, record the Ascendant's foresight choice first. Faction chat is available from the start; visits open only after the choice has been recorded. The two factions have separate visit conversations with the Ascendant. Final commitments end the same faction phase. An older saved session may contain draft records; keep those drafts within the faction and do not use them to brief the Ascendant.

1. Establish assignments, unavailable assets, current articles and lawfully agreed council orders. Invalid Navigation becomes Hold; invalid Security becomes Restraint. No penalty for invalidity alone.

2. Begin the Stability change at -1 for monthly consumption. Check the Warrant using opening Readiness and offered Vigil. A lawful valid Warrant uses Vigil first, gives +1 Stability and guarded status. An unsupported imperial Warrant gives -1; a Warrant outside imperial authority has no effect.
3. Check Guard: unused offered Vigil gives +1 Stability and guarded status. If missing or already used, change Guard to Restraint and add -1 Stability.

4. Fund Navigation. A lodged available Relief lift triggers only for Relief without offered Wayfarer; spend Grey Petrel immediately. Check all other costs. An unfunded order becomes Hold and adds -1 Stability. Prepare Beacon with Maintain +1 and funded Repair +2, capped at 4.

5. Resolve the council voyage against prepared Beacon. Below 2, halt it and add -1 Stability; do not wear Beacon. Otherwise apply Relief +2 or Shared +1 Stability (Military 0), record delivered passage and one crossing wear.

6. Resolve private Trade against the same prepared Beacon. At 3+, or 2 guarded, complete a contract and add one crossing wear. At 2 unguarded, disable Wayfarer, no contract, one wear. Below 2, halt intact with no wear. A reserve Relief voyage and private Trade can both cross.

7. Check each faction’s article duty. NG needs Maintain or funded Repair; NI/NJ need Wayfarer offered; MI/MJ need Spear offered; MA needs Vigil Home; Interim independent Raid breaches army discipline. Add at most one Stability penalty per faction. Loss of an asset does not waive a duty.

8. Resolve Campaign and/or an independent Raid using opening Readiness. A valid council Campaign/Raid without offered Spear adds -1 Stability and no council combat; a separately assigned independent Raid still resolves. Campaign missing delivered Military/Shared passage costs 1 Stability, does not fight and leaves Spear intact. With passage, it costs 1; Readiness 2+ achieves combat, otherwise disable Spear. A Raid costs 1 for disruption; consult its round’s fixed target condition. If target present, Readiness 2+ achieves combat and adds a second Stability cost; below 2 disable Spear without that second loss.

9. Apply the other round-specific hidden conditions printed below, whether purchased or not. Tender cover can prevent only its exact printed crew loss. The council named on a cover is not a substitute for the full condition.

10. Apply one Readiness change: +1 if any qualifying combat occurred, otherwise -1. Final Beacon is prepared Beacon minus actual crossing wear. Add all Stability changes to its opening value. Clamp each final track to 0–4. Mark asset losses, contracts and reserve. Publish consequences and updated signature weights. After round two, expire temporary assignment pledges.

The following are the fixed private answers. The public covers name the primary council and other affected councils, without these descriptive titles or specific choices. These effects happen whether or not the Ascendant buys the card. All four answers concern choices still open when foresight is purchased: unlocked asset assignments and Grey Petrel's task can change during subsequent visits, and council orders and the Warrant are decided later. Standing Commitments, losses and lack of authority may limit a particular intervention. Do not promise that a purchase will be useful or refund it if the relevant option is unavailable.

Shared crosses without protection → If funded Shared passage is delivered and there is no funded Guard or valid Warrant, Lantern’s navigation team is lost. A lodged, available Grey Petrel on Tender cover prevents this loss and is spent.
Shared crosses with protection → A funded Guard or valid Warrant prevents this crew loss. Tender cover does not trigger and stays available.
Shared does not cross → This crew-loss effect does not occur. An unfunded or halted order still has its normal cost.

Shared needs both Wayfarer and Lantern on Council. Passage still needs prepared Beacon 2+. Guard needs offered Vigil; a Warrant also needs imperial authority and opening Readiness 3+. Protection does not repair Beacon or avoid crossing wear.

Wayfarer completes private Trade → A Raid finds the target. At opening Readiness 2+, it fights: total Raid cost Stability −2 and the round’s combat change is Readiness +1. At Readiness 0–1, Spear is disabled: Raid costs Stability −1 and there is no qualifying combat from that Raid.

No completed private Trade → The Raid finds no target. It costs Stability −1, Spear remains intact, and it provides no qualifying combat. Council Relief, Military or Shared passage does not substitute for a private contract.
No Raid → These Raid effects do not occur. Campaign and other orders follow their own rules.

A Trade assignment is not enough: the voyage must complete under the public Beacon and protection rules. If no operation achieves combat, Readiness falls by 1 once. Duty breaches and monthly consumption are additional; tracks stay within 0–4.

Military passage crosses unguarded → Delivered Military passage without funded Guard or valid Warrant causes an extra Stability −1. Protection prevents this extra loss. Grey Petrel’s Tender cover does not protect these stores.

Funded Repair and completed Trade → A funded council Repair together with a completed private Wayfarer Trade gives Stability +1 from distribution. Both must happen. Lantern must be on Council for Repair; Maintain is not Repair.
Neither condition → Neither extra supply effect applies. Relief and Shared receive their normal cargo effects; other cards and ordinary costs still apply.

Repair adds 2 to prepared Beacon, capped at 4, before voyages. Trade must complete. Military needs Wayfarer on Council, so it cannot also make private Trade. These two extra effects cannot both trigger in the same round.

Relief is delivered → A Raid finds the target if the authorised, funded Navigation order is Relief and its voyage actually crosses. Grey Petrel Relief lift counts. At opening Readiness 2+, Raid costs Stability −2 total and achieves combat; at 0–1, Spear is disabled, Raid costs Stability −1 and provides no qualifying combat.

Relief is not delivered → The Raid finds no target, costs Stability −1, leaves Spear intact and provides no qualifying combat. A proposed, unfunded or halted Relief order does not qualify. Shared, Military and private Trade do not qualify.
No Raid → Relief alone does not cause an attack or a Raid penalty. These effects require an actual Raid assignment or funded council Raid.

Combat changes Readiness by +1 once; no successful combat changes it by −1 once. Ordinary cargo, Guard, duty breaches and consumption still apply. A council Raid needs offered Spear; an independent Raid uses its own assignment.

The round-one trial needs spoken agreement from GN+JN+A for Navigation and GS+JS+A for Military. Read back each exact article and its attached terms, independently of the other domain, and record whether it passes. Up to one asset commitment per faction may be attached, with both owners' spoken agreement. Do not quietly detach an unapproved promise to pass its article. No pledge is compulsory. A passed pledge binds only that asset assignment in round two; an informal public plan has no mechanical penalty.

At the Ceremony freeze actual weights. Count both owners’ votes to produce each faction signature; refusal, missing approval or disagreement contributes no support, but the faction’s weight remains in the total. Threshold is ceil(2 × total / 3); at least two signing parties must have positive weight. A zero electorate cannot pass. Count no contracts, verbal concessions or invented influence.

Show the exact final package with five rows, one for each player, and two boxes per row: Assent and Do not assent. Each player ticks one box. A blank row or both boxes ticked gives no assent. If the package fails, permit a replacement within the deadline and use fresh boxes for all five players. Stop on success. If neither of the two permitted packages passes, both provisional articles expire to Interim; no physical state changes. Record dissent even where the weighted package passes. Passing the arithmetic does not establish political consensus.

Cooperation: assets remain scarce, a peaceful month reduces army and Ascendant leverage, and a public ship assignment forgoes a contract. Withheld resources: a directive cannot requisition them automatically. Conflicting orders: check the required decision-makers' agreement before funding. Averted prophecy: a guarded first-round Shared passage or triggered Tender cover prevents the printed crew loss. Failed ratification: expire articles without healing anything.

Ask for starting and ending constitutional preferences and the event that changed them. Ask each player which teammate contribution mattered. For foresight, distinguish assignment changes, changes in the approach to councils, final order changes, bargaining conditions and confidence. A remaining third token is unavoidable if there were two purchases; do not code it as deliberate saving.

The migrated six-agent run found a useful first purchase and a mostly confirmatory second purchase. It did not show deliberate saving or human timing. Do not guide the next Ascendant to repeat that result. Preserve choices before interpreting them.

lore.title: The Void Throne — Lore and Adaptation Record
blocks: The Void Throne — Lore and Adaptation Record

This document records the established setting, explicit author corrections and the five-player adaptation separately. Historical source files are preserved with their original paths and SHA-256 checksums in the repository’s lore/source-inventory.json. This document contains facilitator spoilers from the larger game.
[WORKING] The current prototype borrows the setting and its institutional tensions. It does not silently turn every larger-game subsystem or secret character objective into a rule for the small game.

Roughly two hundred inhabited worlds, stations and habitats make up the Settled Dark. The six dynastic Houses of the Conclave of Thrones governed it for three millennia. The Ascendant broke their order over a conquest beginning sixty years ago; the last loyalist fleet broke at Pale Meridian eleven months before the original Charter Day. The source describes the Ascendant as ninety-six years old. Source: archive/legacy-lore/Setting.md.

The Charter negotiations take place at the Seam. The proposed empire is the Settled Dominion. The Charter is unfinished and contested; the original wider game includes the Houses, Administratum, Ecclesiatum and other institutions. The phrase “sixtieth year of the Settled Peace” sits beside the recently completed conquest in the source; preserve that phrasing as a chronology question rather than inventing a correction.

Guild navigators make interstellar travel possible by sensing the immaterial deep. The Guild’s indispensability is its political leverage. Navigation Rights Petition GUILD-14 has waited fourteen years for a response. Licensing, discretion and the unresolved scope of “associated services” matter; the Guild is not canonically a civilian-first charity. Source: Factions/Ductus Guild.md and Game/The Charter of Settlement.md.

Facilitator-only larger-game lore: navigation is reception of a transmission, not merely innate talent. Its character has changed. Different Guild characters know different pieces of the change, unexplored routes and possible communications. This prototype omits that information puzzle and its individual secrets; it does not refute them.

The Janissariat’s three billion psychically conditioned warriors made conquest possible. Conditioning is designed for war and frays in peacetime. The constitutional question is whether the army is a sacred autonomous order, an imperial instrument, or another institution subject to negotiated oversight. The original High Command has internal disagreements; this prototype replaces secret individual victory conditions with shared faction priorities. Source: Factions/Janissariat High Command.md.

Facilitator-only larger-game lore: conditioning derives from early Ductus research and suppresses a perceptual capability. Fraying can release that perception in people trained to treat it as a threat. It is not simply physical illness, moral decline or guaranteed peacefulness. Source: Lore/Fraying Conditioning Thread.md.

Explicit author clarification in this design conversation: not fighting costs combat power, creating an incentive for aggressive choices others may dislike. The Ascendant has their loyalty while they fight and needs a viable army while seeking a better future. In the prototype, qualifying combat sustains Readiness; peaceful rounds reduce it. This does not establish automatic treason after one quiet month.
The Ascendant and the Throne Eternal

The Ascendant wants an empire that deserves to exist and a settlement that avoids future succession wars. The source depicts Communion as a process of transformation and uncertainty about whether they can verify their own goodness. Older mechanics include Tarot, Clarity and conditional orders. Those are historical mechanics, not the present small-game rules. Source: The Ascendant.md.

The Throne Eternal is the Ecclesiatum’s name for something ancient and directional, not simply a conventional benevolent god. Facilitator-only records distinguish discovery from a managed religious interpretation; its destination is uncertain. Source: The Throne Eternal.md.

Explicit author clarification: using foresight diminishes the Ascendant’s power; unspent foresight should contribute to settlement leverage. The Ascendant need not remain in control if they can trust the final government to govern without them. The three-token budget and weighted signature formula are prototype implementations of this instruction, not claims about a universal magical exchange rate.
The Narrow and the prototype inventions

The Narrow is an established strategic corridor linking inner systems and the southern rim, with a waystation council that has governed for thirty generations. Sorenne's Fall in the Southern Houses Arm provides the civilian stakes for this prototype. Vethis Secundus remains a different setting location whose resistance is collective non-cooperation; it is not the armed opponent here. Sources: Systems/Vethis Cluster.md; Systems/Southern Houses Arm.md.

Established setting: Sorenne's Fall is a star system of forty million people living beneath a battle debris field. Its former colonial administration continued governing after orders stopped arriving. The Sorenne Flag scattered rather than surrender at Pale Meridian and has been bringing the system irregular supplies. Campaign Ash pursues House Sorenne's surviving fleet. Sources: Systems/Southern Houses Arm.md and Game/Fringe Campaigns.md.

Scenario adaptation: the current crisis makes the Narrow the supply passage serving Sorenne's Fall. Stability replaces the former Communities label and records supplies and functioning civil services on the same 0–4 scale, with the same starting value and numerical effects. The Flag anchorage beyond the crossing, local patrol, traffic-linked appearances, named assets and two-month timetable are scenario additions. No value on Stability implies political loyalty or turns the system's civilians into military targets.

Beacon measures service infrastructure. Guild work prepares it; military protection addresses named physical attacks and exposed berths. Guard does not repair a psychic relationship with the void. Grey Petrel already has a contracted licensed pilot; the Ascendant never conjures a navigator.

The small game settles two outstanding instruments within a wider Charter. Nonplayed institutions are assumed to have accepted all six permitted alternatives and to provide formalities including sanctification. This removes a surprise veto without rewriting their broader canonical importance. The weighted final vote is a design adaptation, not the original Charter’s full legitimacy mechanism.

Factions decide together; no individual secret objectives are required. Every faction has independent choices that can create risk and reward without another faction’s consent. Legal restrictions and physical capability are separate. Cooperation should involve actual compromise, not an automatic best outcome for everyone.

A lost commercial contract is an acute opportunity cost. A surviving ship returns after useful service. Do not remove ownership leverage merely because an asset was committed. Readiness contributes both Janissariat and Ascendant leverage; unspent foresight contributes only to the latter. Three foresight tokens, at most two purchases, implies a minimum one-token remainder.

The first five-player plan used unanimous final ratification. Later author-approved experiments replaced that with weighted party signatures; the current draft uses the latter. Trial articles still require the three relevant consents. This distinction must survive all future exports.
Open questions and material outside this prototype

Still to establish through play: whether cooperation’s concessions are sufficiently even; whether a party chooses NONE; whether weighted ratification over army dissent produces a credible government; whether the six-minute trial phase fits human play; whether Military autonomy or joint authority is attractive when actually tested.

The larger conspiracy, Houses, Clarity transformation, succession forgery, five Pillars, strategic map, hidden transmissions and pre-human structures remain historical setting material outside this small scenario. They are preserved in the source archive, not introduced through surprise adjudication.

The separate GameSpec attempt describes a 24–30-player game and treats its source directory as canonical within that project. It is preserved under archive/legacy-gamespec as an older design line. This migration creates a separate Playtrace repository; it does not claim to validate or rewrite that GameSpec package.

playtest.title: The Void Throne — Revised Visions Playtest and Migration Report
blocks: The Void Throne — Revised Visions Playtest and Migration Report

[WORKING] The hypothesis was that public intentions and clearly scoped vision covers would let the Ascendant buy information relevant to live choices while retaining a meaningful option to preserve power. One fresh six-agent run used five player roles and an independent facilitator, with the same personalities as the preceding weighted-settlement test.

The source record has 113 contributions across eleven phases and six debriefs. Each role authored its own choices. Scoped packets separated faction discussions, councils and the purchased vision. Times represent the proposed paper schedule, not measured human play. The migration adds a deterministic Playtrace replay of those decisions; it is not another independent LLM run.
Round one: information changed the plan

The Guild displayed Trade/Maintain and Hold/Guard. The army wanted Military/Campaign; the Ascendant initially proposed those orders with a Warrant. With no offered Wayfarer for military passage, the Ascendant bought the Security vision to investigate Raid.

The answer tied a successful Raid target appearance to completed private Trade. The Ascendant disclosed it and offered Grey Petrel for Relief. All four faction players changed council requests; the Ascendant changed Military/Campaign to reserve Relief/Raid, retaining Warrant. Asset assignments did not change. Information and the material reserve offer arrived together, so the result does not isolate the information’s causal effect.

Result: Beacon 1, Communities 3, Readiness 4, all faction assets intact, one contract, reserve spent, two foresight left. Two crossings wore the route. The Guild secured NG provisionally with a Lantern Council pledge. MA failed because the Guild Security delegate refused it; the Ascendant had approved the trial.
Round two: relevance without a major order change

The live plan paired funded Repair and private Trade. The Ascendant bought the Navigation answer, learning the extra Communities +1 when that combination completes. The Ascendant retained Repair/Guard/no Warrant; both Guild players retained their choices and reported greater confidence. Army requests moved from Restraint with Warrant to Guard without Warrant as protection coordination. No asset assignment changed.

Result: Beacon 2, Communities 4, Readiness 3, all faction assets intact, two contracts, reserve spent, one foresight left. The peaceful round reduced both army and Ascendant signature weight. The Guild’s concession was tender service and upkeep; it did not lose a commercial contract in this run.
Settlement and the unanswered saving question

Final weights were Guild 4, Janissariat 3 and Ascendant 4; 8 of 11 was required. NG/MJ passed with both Guild players and the Ascendant approving, despite both army players refusing. Operational cooperation did not produce constitutional consensus.

The Ascendant bought both available rounds’ visions. They did not choose NONE. The third token remained because only two purchases were allowed. In debrief they judged the second purchase less useful in practice and said declining would have been defensible; that was hindsight, not a decision observed in play.

With the same physical ending but one purchase declined, Ascendant weight would be 5 and the threshold would still be 8. An Ascendant–Janissariat coalition would then be arithmetically possible. This is a counterfactual calculation, not an alternative simulated ballot or evidence that they would agree.

Independent checks reproduced both operational resolutions, provisional signatures and pledges, foresight payment and disclosure order, final weights and all five final votes. The report retains original contributions, side-by-side drafts/final faction sheets, council sheets, state changes and private answers actually delivered.

The strongest finding is a useful first purchase. The second is evidence of confirmation and coordination rather than a second major change. There is no evidence of deliberate saving, human pacing, all alternative constitutions, or assignment changes after disclosure. One run cannot establish balance or isolate all procedure changes from fresh choices.

Playtrace stores a source snapshot, executable model audit, deterministic replay and hypothesis-linked evidence. The replay is context for the hypothesis, not new evidence that foresight changes player psychology. The existing six-agent record is preserved intact; mechanical replay must not rewrite its statements.

Run the paper prototype with people and record purchase decisions before answers. Compare initial and final constitutional preferences. Test a council arrangement other than NG/Interim. Observe whether the first package’s agenda-setting advantage matters and whether passing over a dissenting army feels like a workable settlement.

The local browser lets one tester control every seat, try refusal, conflict, poor directives, averted visions and failed ballots, and export the complete record. It automatically applies consequences but does not substitute for multiplayer negotiation.

Migration checks: twenty rules and integration tests passed. Browser controls reproduced the recorded ending, saved debrief notes, exported and resumed decisions, and preserved damage after failed ratification. These are software verification results, not additional human or LLM playtests.

project.title: The Void Throne — Project Index and Working Agreement
blocks: The Void Throne — Project Index and Working Agreement

The Void Throne now has a separate local game repository at C:/AnalogueGames/void-throne and a dedicated Google Drive folder. The older Obsidian and GameSpec folders remain untouched. Their relevant sources are preserved in the new repository with checksums.

[WORKING] The current design is the five-player, two-round paper prototype with revised vision timing, three foresight tokens, voluntary Standing Commitments and weighted final settlement. The browser and Playtrace are development tools; neither is required to play the paper game.

Drive: editable player rulebook, facilitator guide, lore/adaptation record and playtest write-up. Local docs are initial publication sources and offline copies. Read current Drive revisions before republishing changes; there is no automatic two-way synchronisation.

Repository: game-owned engine and browser interface, external Playtrace plugin, manifest, hypotheses, evidence, tests, captured document revisions and original simulation records. Shared Playtrace remains at C:/Coding/playtrace and contains no new Void Throne design state.
Archive: original development reports and printable packs, the larger-game lore and the previous GameSpec source. Historical versions remain labelled; they are not a second current ruleset.

Run launch.py from the repository, or use Start Playtest.cmd. The local browser opens at http://127.0.0.1:8877. Control every seat, record reasons, commit assets, enter council orders and cast votes. It saves the last completed sheet locally. Download HTML and JSON before starting another test. You can resume an exported decision record.

Run playtrace_game.py reproduce using the Playtrace Python environment to build the source snapshot, deterministic replay, report and hypothesis-linked experiment bundle. Run the game’s tests before changing printed consequences. The exact command and dependency path are in README.md.

For a fresh LLM game, use the information-boundary protocol in design/experiments/agent-protocol.md and record original decisions. The retained six-agent run is ready for inspection; a deterministic replay is not a fresh conversation.

Will the Ascendant deliberately decline a purchase? Does the army accept a settlement imposed by a valid weighted coalition? Do provisional powers change preferences, or merely confirm them? Does the Guild sacrifice enough in the reserve-supported path? Can people finish the discussion and signatures on time?
The current code implements the accepted experimental rules. New balance proposals remain proposals until the designer chooses them. No statistical claim of success follows from one agent run.

The Void Throne — Facilitator Guide, draft v0.3: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1402miaVHlXY84ND4YshuEOZqCT07ELe2qtKWgYMcS4M/edit?usp=drivesdk

briefs.title: The Void Throne — Player Briefs
blocks: Give the Guild and Janissariat players their faction’s shared brief. Give the Ascendant their own brief. Read these alongside the player rulebook.
Two players · shared assets and objectives. Your Navigation delegate is GN; your Security delegate is GS.

Use the faction phase to agree asset assignments and negotiating priorities with your teammate. Stay at your own table; do not speak or send messages to the other faction. The Ascendant may visit after making their foresight choice. You may discuss proposals with them and revise unlocked assignments until the phase ends. Both players then confirm the same assignments aloud and record them without signatures. Take your approach to the councils yourselves, without written instructions.

You operate the passage service through the Narrow. Wayfarer is your freight vessel; Lantern carries your navigation team and maintains the route. Those ships are needed for civilian supplies, military transport and your own commercial obligations.

Your petition, GUILD-14, asks the Charter to recognise the Guild's navigation rights. Each Navigation article answers it differently: Guild discretion leaves priorities with you, Imperial priority places them with the Ascendant, and Joint authorisation gives both factions a say.
Keep Lantern's navigators alive and finish with Beacon at least 2.
Secure Guild navigation rights, preferably through Guild discretion.
Complete two commercial contracts, one in each round.
Leave Sorenne's Fall with Stability at least 2.

Offering Wayfarer for public service means missing that month's contract. The ship returns if it survives, but the opportunity has gone. You may accept that cost for relief, protection or a worthwhile constitutional concession.
Two players · shared assets and objectives. Your Navigation delegate is JN; your Security delegate is JS.

Use the faction phase to agree asset assignments and negotiating priorities with your teammate. Stay at your own table; do not speak or send messages to the other faction. The Ascendant may visit after making their foresight choice. You may discuss proposals with them and revise unlocked assignments until the phase ends. Both players then confirm the same assignments aloud and record them without signatures. Take your approach to the councils yourselves, without written instructions.

You command Spear, the 9th Pale Cohort, and Vigil, the Narrow garrison. Spear has local assault craft, but needs Guild transport to campaign beyond the crossing. Vigil can protect traffic or remain at its institutional bases.

The Sorenne Flag gives you an enemy to fight. The difficulty is finding it without further damaging the system you are supposed to secure. An unsuccessful expedition still consumes supplies and disrupts civilian traffic, while doing nothing to sustain your conditioning.
Keep Spear intact and finish with Readiness at least 3, preferably 4.
Secure the army's constitutional position, preferably through Military autonomy.
Protect your soldiers from operations they cannot sustain. At opening Readiness below 2, combat disables Spear.
Leave Sorenne's Fall with Stability at least 2.

Military autonomy lets you choose operations, but requires Vigil to stay Home. Joint authorisation gives the Guild a say over military orders. Imperial command leaves the Ascendant able to order you to stand down.

One player · A on decision sheets. Attend Security and Government; tell Navigation and Supply your decision in person when you hold its authority. A council member records the final order; no signature is needed.

You need a government capable of maintaining the Dominion, and an army capable of defending it. A quiet month may help Sorenne's Fall while weakening both the Janissariat and the authority they give you.

You begin with imperial command, three foresight tokens and one contracted service from the cutter Grey Petrel. Spending foresight gives you information about the crisis, but reduces your weight in the final settlement.
Ratify a settlement with Beacon at least 1, Stability at least 2 and Readiness at least 2.
Keep Readiness at least 3 and Spear intact where the cost is acceptable.
Establish a government you can trust to govern without your constant intervention.
Account for the people and institutions that paid for that settlement.
You gain no special success from keeping imperial command. Use the provisional government to find out whether delegation works, then judge the final Charter on that evidence.

Use your worksheet to record your foresight choice and Grey Petrel's task during faction discussion, and your final Warrant choice during councils. Tell the councils your decisions in person; you do not need to write instructions or sign an order. Your authority over council decisions follows the current Charter articles, described in the Component Reference.
The Ascendant starts with three foresight tokens. Each unspent token adds one to their final settlement weight.

At the start of each faction phase, choose your foresight before visiting either faction or hearing its plans for this round. Read the two covers: Navigation and Supply, and Security and Government. They identify the council at the centre of each prophecy and any other council it could affect. They do not reveal the action, condition, risk or reward. Choose one answer and pay one token before opening it, or choose NONE and retain your token. You may use the public state, existing commitments and anything learned in earlier phases to make this choice.

There is at most one purchase per round. Your choice must reach the facilitator before you visit a faction and before the faction phase ends. A missing, multiple or late choice means NONE. Choosing NONE also completes your choice and permits visits. Tokens do not recover, and there are no swaps, refunds or further purchases that month. Waiting to choose leaves less time for visits; it does not extend the phase.

The facilitator announces the expenditure and remaining tokens. The chosen card and its answer remain private unless the Ascendant shares them. You may show, describe, conceal or misrepresent the answer; the facilitator will not certify your claims to other players.
An answer states what happens if its conditions occur. It does not tell you what players will choose or cover every possible risk. Those conditions apply whether anyone reads the card or not.

While you choose, the two factions discuss privately with their own teammates. After your choice is recorded, you may visit either faction, return to one you visited earlier, relay offers and share or withhold your vision. Each visit is a conversation with that faction; do not bring the two factions together. Until the phase ends, factions can revise unlocked assignments and you can revise Grey Petrel's task. Existing Standing Commitments remain binding. Council orders and your Warrant are decided in the council phase. Avoiding a vision's condition averts its result; it does not make the vision false.

Example: you choose the Navigation prophecy before hearing the Guild's plan. During a later visit, you discover they intend a voyage mentioned in the answer. You can explain its consequences and ask for a different assignment or protection. The cover did not promise that their plan would make this prophecy useful. A lost asset or a Standing Commitment may limit what can change; spending a token does not guarantee a useful intervention.
There are three tokens and at most one purchase in each of the two rounds. At least one token will remain. Keeping more requires choosing NONE in at least one round.
The Warrant draws on the Ascendant's authority over the army to use Vigil independently of the council's other operation.
Requirement: Military authority is Interim or Imperial command, opening Readiness is at least 3, and Vigil is offered to Council.
Timing: record the final Warrant before the council bell.
Effect: use Vigil first; Stability +1 and guarded status. Security may use offered Spear for a separate order.

Under Interim or Imperial command, a Warrant without sufficient Readiness or offered Vigil fails and costs Stability 1. Under Military autonomy or Joint authorisation, it is advice only, with no effect or penalty. A missing or unconfirmed Warrant means No.
If a valid Warrant uses Vigil, a simultaneous Guard lacks its asset and pays the normal failure cost.

Grey Petrel is a contracted cutter with a licensed Guild pilot and a protection detail. Its contract covers one triggered intervention during the whole game. It cannot carry Spear, repair Beacon or provide a second service after its token is spent.
Before the faction bell, lodge Relief lift, Tender cover or Keep. The task locks before councils. If its condition does not occur, retain the reserve token.

Relief lift triggers when the final authorised Navigation order is Relief and Wayfarer was not offered. Grey Petrel supplies the ship requirement and spends the token immediately, even if low Beacon later halts the voyage. Wayfarer may still make a private Trade voyage.

Tender cover triggers in round one when Shared is delivered unguarded and the printed crew-loss consequence occurs. Prevent that loss of Lantern's team and spend the token. This gives no general protection or track bonus and has no round-two trigger.
Keep retains the token without intervening. A missing task also means Keep. Unspent reserve gives no settlement weight.

components.title: The Void Throne — Component Reference
blocks: Use this document during play alongside the Player Rulebook and your faction brief. It contains the rules text for asset cards, track references, council sheets and Charter cards. The Ascendant's foresight, Warrant and reserve rules are in their Player Brief.
Beacon records the condition of the Narrow's maintained navigation and service infrastructure. It starts at 2 and runs from 0 to 4.
Maintain adds 1 and funded Repair adds 2 before crossings. This produces prepared Beacon, capped at 4. Every voyage uses that same prepared value; crossing wear is deducted afterwards.

Stability records whether the system's forty million people can obtain supplies and keep their civil services operating. Relief and protection improve it. Disrupted traffic, fighting, failed commitments and monthly consumption reduce it.
The track starts at 3 and runs from 0 to 4:
4 — Secure: supplies are reliable and services can meet immediate needs.
3 — Functioning: the administration is keeping the system supplied.
2 — Strained: shortages are affecting daily life.
1 — Failing: severe shortages are disrupting essential services.
0 — Emergency: the system cannot meet its immediate needs without relief.
These descriptions explain the track; they add no further bonuses or penalties. Stability is not loyalty to the Ascendant. People can be well supplied and still oppose the new government.
Readiness measures the combat effectiveness of the Janissariat force. It starts at 3 and runs from 0 to 4. Use its value at the start of the round—opening Readiness—for combat and Warrant checks.
If an operation achieves qualifying combat, Readiness rises by 1 once for the round. Otherwise it falls by 1 once. Food, Guard, Home and unsuccessful expeditions do not sustain conditioning.
Assign Wayfarer to Council or Trade.
Council offers the vessel for Relief, Military or Shared passage. It cannot also Trade.
Trade attempts this round's commercial voyage without council permission. Success completes one contract.

Trade succeeds at prepared Beacon 3 or 4, or at 2 if guarded. At 2 without protection, Wayfarer is attacked and disabled: no contract is completed, but the attempted crossing still causes one Beacon wear.
Below prepared Beacon 2, the ship does not depart. It stays intact, completes no contract and causes no wear. A successful Trade voyage causes one wear.
There is one contract available each round. Record completed contracts, but do not spend or transfer them. A missed contract cannot be recovered by making two private voyages next round.
Assign Lantern to Maintain or Council.
Maintain adds 1 to prepared Beacon without needing a council order.
Council offers Lantern for Repair or Shared. The council must still choose that order.
Lantern cannot do both. If its navigation team is lost, the asset is unavailable for the rest of the game; you cannot replace the crew during these two months.
Assign Spear to Council, Raid or Stand down.
Council offers Spear for a council Campaign or Raid.
Raid launches an independent interception of a Sorenne Flag patrol, using Spear's own local craft.
Stand down leaves Spear undeployed, with no recovery or Readiness bonus.
An independent Raid needs agreement from both faction members but no other party's permission. It cannot also supply a council operation. A disabled Spear cannot act again.
Assign Vigil to Council or Home.
Council offers Vigil for Guard or an eligible imperial Warrant. A Warrant has first claim on its use.
Home keeps Vigil protecting institutional bases. It grants no track bonus, but fulfils the Military autonomy duty.
Vigil remains intact throughout the game and can perform only one task each round. It cannot supply both Guard and a Warrant.

Council is an offer of service for the round, not a transfer of ownership. A surviving asset returns for its next assignment and retains its ownership weight at the Ceremony. Its owner has given up the other use it could have had that month.
Losses are permanent for this game. None of the available actions restores a disabled Wayfarer, replaces Lantern's navigators or restores Spear. Repair works on Beacon.

Funded Guard or a valid Warrant makes traffic guarded for the round. Either protects against the specified physical threats and permits Trade at prepared Beacon 2. Neither raises Beacon, allows a crossing below 2 or removes normal wear.
Each actual crossing costs one Beacon after preparation. Grey Petrel can carry Relief while Wayfarer Trades, producing two crossings. Both check the same prepared Beacon value.
Choose one order. An offered asset is one its owner assigned to Council on the binding faction sheet. First check the assets; for a voyage, then check prepared Beacon.
Cost: offered Wayfarer, or a triggered Grey Petrel Relief lift.
Effect: deliver supplies to Sorenne's Fall; Stability +2; one Beacon wear.
Relief does not carry Spear for a Campaign. Grey Petrel can substitute for this voyage only.
Effect: deliver military passage for a Campaign against the Sorenne Flag's anchorage; one Beacon wear.
Military gives no supply bonus. Security must also choose Campaign and have offered Spear before a Campaign takes place.
Cost: Wayfarer and Lantern both offered to Council.
Effect: deliver civilian and military cargo; Stability +1; military passage; one Beacon wear.
Shared is one crossing. Lantern is committed to that voyage and cannot also Maintain. Scenario conditions may expose its navigation team to additional risk.
Effect: prepared Beacon +2, capped at 4, before crossings.
Repair makes no crossing and carries no council cargo. Wayfarer may still Trade privately through the repaired route.
Effect: no council voyage or repair.
Private Trade, Maintain and an independent Raid still resolve if assigned.
An authorised order without its required assets becomes Hold and costs Stability 1. Shared pays this failure cost once even if both assets are missing.

A funded Relief, Military or Shared voyage facing prepared Beacon below 2 is halted. Lose Stability 1, deliver no cargo or passage, and cause no crossing wear. An unfunded order has already become Hold, so it does not also pay this halted-voyage cost.
Example: the Ascendant chooses Military, but the Guild assigned Wayfarer to Trade. Military becomes Hold and costs Stability 1. The private Trade voyage is still checked normally.
Choose one order. An independent Raid and an eligible Warrant may also occur, using their own requirements. No asset can be used twice.
Cost: offered Spear and delivered Military or Shared passage.
Effect: attack the Sorenne Flag's anchorage beyond the Narrow; Stability −1 from disruption to Sorenne's Fall's supply traffic.
At opening Readiness at least 2, the Campaign achieves qualifying combat. Below 2, Spear is disabled and achieves no qualifying combat.
Without delivered military passage, the Campaign does not leave. It costs Stability 1, leaves Spear intact and achieves no combat. A Relief voyage cannot carry the cohort.
Cost: offered Spear for a council Raid, or Spear assigned to an independent Raid.
Effect: seek a Sorenne Flag patrol on this side of the crossing; Stability −1 for disruption, even if no patrol appears.
No Guild ship is needed. The patrol's appearance depends on a fixed concealed condition for that round. The facilitator applies that condition; there is no dice roll.

If the patrol is absent, Spear remains intact and achieves no combat. If it appears at opening Readiness at least 2, the Raid achieves combat and costs one further Stability: −2 in total. If it appears below 2, Spear is disabled, with no second Stability loss and no qualifying combat.
Foresight may reveal the condition. Traffic alone does not cause a Raid: Spear must actually have a Raid assignment or a funded council Raid order.
Cost: offered Vigil, not already used by a Warrant.
Effect: protect civilian traffic and service installations; Stability +1 and guarded status.
Guard does not qualify as combat and does not repair Beacon.
An independently assigned Raid still proceeds.

A valid council Raid or Campaign without offered Spear becomes Restraint and costs Stability 1. Guard without unused offered Vigil does the same. A separately assigned independent Raid still resolves and pays its own costs.

Example: Spear is assigned to independent Raid, but Security authorises Campaign. Campaign fails because Spear was not offered to Council. The Raid still occurs. Its costs and the failed Campaign's penalty both apply.

At the end of the round, raise Readiness by 1 if any operation achieved qualifying combat; otherwise lower it by 1. Apply this change once, keeping Readiness within 0–4. An expedition that fails to reach a fight does not qualify.

The first round ends with a chance to try a new government. Choose who can direct each council and what duties come with that authority. The articles that pass govern round two and cannot be revoked or replaced during it.

An article gives authority and imposes a legal service duty. It does not transfer ownership of an asset. A faction can disobey a duty, take the printed penalty and carry out any otherwise possible independent action.
A Standing Commitment goes further: both owners bind a particular assignment for round two. Use it when another party wants a dependable offer of service before accepting an article.

Under the starting arrangement, the Ascendant chooses both council orders and may issue an eligible Warrant. The Guild has no service duty. An independent Janissariat Raid breaks discipline and costs Stability 1 in addition to the Raid's ordinary costs.
Guild discretion (NG): the Guild Navigation delegate chooses the order. The Guild must assign Lantern to Maintain or provide a funded Repair. Otherwise Stability falls by 1. Wayfarer may Trade.
Imperial priority (NI): the Ascendant chooses the order. The Guild must offer Wayfarer to Council or lose Stability 1. The ship forgoes Trade even if the council leaves it unused.
Joint authorisation (NJ): both Navigation delegates must agree the same order, or Navigation Holds. The Guild must offer Wayfarer to Council or lose Stability 1.
Offering Lantern without a funded Repair does not fulfil Guild discretion's upkeep duty. Grey Petrel providing Relief does not fulfil the Wayfarer duty under Imperial priority or Joint authorisation.

Imperial command (MI): the Ascendant chooses Security's order and retains eligible Warrant power. The Janissariat must offer Spear to Council or lose Stability 1. The Ascendant may still choose not to fight.

Military autonomy (MA): the Janissariat Security delegate chooses the order. The Janissariat must keep Vigil Home or lose Stability 1. There is no imperial Warrant. An independent Raid is permitted if Vigil stays Home.
Joint authorisation (MJ): both Security delegates must agree the same order, or Security uses Restraint. The Janissariat must offer Spear to Council or lose Stability 1. There is no imperial Warrant.

Each faction takes at most one article-duty penalty per round. Lost assets do not waive a duty. Duty penalties are separate from failed orders, Raid costs and monthly consumption: the civil administration's supply and protection arrangements can be disrupted in more than one way.

Navigation needs the Guild Navigation delegate, Janissariat Navigation delegate and Ascendant to agree the same exact proposal. Military needs the Guild Security delegate, Janissariat Security delegate and Ascendant. State agreement aloud to the facilitator; no signatures are needed.
The two articles are decided independently. One may pass while the other stays Interim. Agreeing an article does not by itself bind an asset promise made by your teammate.
Each faction may attach one available asset assignment to one exact article proposal. Both teammates must approve it. Permitted assignments are:

Record the owner, asset, assignment and article, then ask both teammates to confirm the commitment aloud. If either owner does not agree, that article fails as proposed. To remove or change the promise, agree revised terms and obtain the necessary agreement again.

An article can pass without a commitment. A valid commitment activates only if its article passes. It then overrides contrary round-two selections and defaults, and expires after the round's operation.
The assignment is binding; the council's future order is not. An announced plan creates no extra mechanical penalty if the authorised council later chooses something else.

Example: the Guild attaches Lantern Council to a Joint military proposal. Both Guild players approve the promise; both Security delegates and the Ascendant approve the article. Lantern is now locked to Council next round, but Navigation must still decide whether to use it for Repair or Shared.
An unconfirmed, ambiguous or unauthorised Navigation order becomes Hold. The equivalent Security order becomes Restraint. Under a joint article, conflicting choices count as disagreement.
There is no penalty merely for lacking a valid order. An authorised order that lacks its assets does incur the printed failure cost. Private assignments and duties apply in either case.
